# Game model (painting/press puzzle)

## Screen
- Top-left framed picture = TARGET image the canvas must match.
- Top toolbar = color swatches; the one with a white underline is selected. Click a swatch (ACTION6) to select that paint color; the press instantly takes that color.
- Center: a CANVAS (grid, ~10x11 cells) and a PRESS (gray-framed block of paint) that sits on one side of the canvas.

## Mechanics
- ACTION5 = press/stamp: the press plunges into the canvas from the side it occupies and repaints the nearest HALF of the canvas (5 of 10 rows for a top/bottom press) with the selected color. Pressing again from the same side has no further effect.
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move the press one step around the canvas along an 8-position ring
  (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW). The action names the compass direction of the step:
  e.g. from N, ACTION4 (east) -> NE; from NE, ACTION4 is blocked, ACTION2 (south) -> E.
  Moves that would leave the ring do nothing.
- Diagonal positions presumably stamp a diagonal half (untested).

## Strategy
Decide which side each color must come from, then travel around the ring, select color, press.
Ring distance N<->S = 4 steps. Order colors so that the last press covers the smaller/last region.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
# Game model (paint-press puzzle)

## Screen
- Top-left framed picture = TARGET image the 10x10 canvas must match exactly.
- Top toolbar = color swatches; white underline marks the selected color. ACTION6 on a swatch
  sets the paint color of ALL presses (paint supply is global).
- Center: CANVAS (10x10 cells, 8px each; at x216-296, y272-352) plus one or more PRESSES
  stacked on the same side of the canvas (big one nearest the canvas, smaller ones behind).

## Mechanics
- ACTION1/2/3/4 move the whole press stack one step around an 8-position ring
  (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW). The action names the compass direction of the step:
  from N, ACTION4(east)->NE, then ACTION2(south)->E, ACTION2->SE, ACTION3(west)->S, etc.
  Steps that would leave the ring do nothing. N<->S is 4 steps.
- ACTION5 fires the FRONT (big) press. ACTION6 clicked on a specific press fires THAT press.
- Firing stamps a rectangle of the selected color onto the canvas from that side:
  - Big press (paint block 10 wide x 7 tall) from N/E/S/W paints the nearest 5 rows/columns
    (half the canvas, full width).
  - Big press from a diagonal position paints the 55-cell triangular half on that side
    (e.g. from SE: all cells with row+col >= 9).
  - Small press (paint block 4 wide x 3 tall) paints a 4x3 block at its aligned columns,
    3 deep from its side. Painted footprint = press paint-block footprint.
- Paint overwrites; later stamps cover earlier ones. Plan stamp ORDER accordingly
  (big background halves first, small details last).

## Method
1. Read the target grid with read_pixels (region x22,y26,80x80, 10x10 samples).
2. Decompose it into press stamps + order.
3. Walk the ring, set color, fire (ACTION5 for big, ACTION6-click for a smaller press).

[After action · write GUIDE.md]
# Paint-press puzzle — solved model (6 levels, WIN)

## Screen
- Top-left framed picture = TARGET the 10x10 canvas must match. Read it with
  read_pixels region (x22,y26,80x80), 10 rows x 10 cols → exact cell colors.
- Top toolbar = color swatches (up to 7: white, purple, orange, yellow, green, red, blue),
  centers y=36, x = 188, 236, 284, 332, 380, 428, 476. White underline = selected.
  ACTION6 on a swatch sets the paint color of ALL presses (global paint), except the tiny
  2-wide "cap" press which stays white.
- Canvas: 10x10 cells of 8px at x216-296, y272-352 (cell (r,c) center ≈ (220+8c, 276+8r)).
- Press stack sits on one side of the canvas: big press (10 wide x 7 block) in front,
  4-wide x 3-deep press behind it, plus a 2-wide white cap press.

## Mechanics
- ACTION1/2/3/4 move the whole stack one step around an 8-position ring
  (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW); the action = compass direction of the step
  (1=N, 2=S, 3=W, 4=E). Illegal steps do nothing. N<->S = 4 steps.
- ACTION5 fires the big press. ACTION6 clicked on a press fires THAT press
  (4-wide press: at N click ≈ (256,172); at W click ≈ (112,307)).
- Stamps (paint overwrites; last stamp wins):
  - Big press from N/S/E/W: nearest half → 5 rows/columns, full width.
  - Big press from a corner: the 55-cell diagonal half, e.g. SE = {r+c >= 9},
    NW = {r+c <= 9}, SW = {c <= r}, NE = {c >= r}. Corner stamps share the boundary
    diagonal, so the later one owns it.
  - 4-wide press: 4x3 block centered on its edge (N → rows0-2 x cols3-6;
    W → rows3-6 x cols0-2). At a corner it would give a 10-cell corner triangle.

## Solving method (fast)
1. Read target grid. 2. Express it as a small ordered stack of the above stamp shapes,
   using large halves as the base and small blocks last; a region equal to
   (shapeA minus shapeB) means A is stamped before B.
3. Route the ring to minimize moves; group stamps that share a ring position.
Typical solution: 3-5 stamps, ~13-20 actions per level.

[After action · message]
Completed the game (6/6 levels, state = **WIN**) in 92 turns.

**The game model I built:**
- The top-left picture is a target for a 10×10 canvas; a stack of "presses" orbits the canvas on an 8-position ring (arrows = compass steps).
- ACTION5 fires the big press; clicking a press with ACTION6 fires that specific press; clicking a toolbar swatch sets the global paint color.
- Stamp shapes: big press = nearest half (5 rows/cols) from an edge, or a 55-cell diagonal half from a corner; the 4-wide press = a centered 4×3 block.
- Paint overwrites, so each level is solved by decomposing the target into an *ordered* stack of these shapes (big halves first, small blocks last) and routing the ring efficiently.

Key discoveries along the way: arrows only appeared inert at first because the canvas was uniform (level 1); color selection is global to all presses (level 3); and clicking a press fires it, which unlocked the smaller press (levels 3–6).
